author.name: Elena Park, MD, MS, FACMG
author.practice: Riverview Cancer Institute — Hereditary Cancer Clinic

sections.reasonForReferral: Maria is a 58-year-old woman referred for cancer genetics evaluation after a new diagnosis of invasive ductal carcinoma of the right breast. The purpose of the visit is to assess hereditary cancer risk and determine whether germline testing could inform her care.
sections.oncologicHistory: A screening mammogram identified a 2.7 cm mass in the upper-outer quadrant of the right breast. Ultrasound-guided core biopsy performed on 2026-06-30 showed grade 3 invasive ductal carcinoma. Estrogen receptor and progesterone receptor staining were both less than 1%, and HER2 immunohistochemistry was 1+ (negative). She has no prior history of cancer.
sections.personalMedicalHistory: Medical history is notable for well-controlled hypertension. The uterus and ovaries are intact. She has not previously had germline cancer-susceptibility testing.
sections.familyHistory: Her mother is alive at age 81 with no cancer history. Her father died at age 74 from myocardial infarction. One brother, age 55, has no cancer history. A maternal aunt was diagnosed with lung cancer at age 76 after a long smoking history. There is no known breast, ovarian, pancreatic, prostate, colorectal, or endometrial cancer in first- or second-degree relatives. The family is not known to be of Ashkenazi Jewish ancestry.
sections.pathologySummary: Right breast core biopsy PATH-88421 documents invasive ductal carcinoma, Nottingham grade 3. ER is negative (<1%), PR is negative (<1%), and HER2 is negative (IHC 1+).
sections.assessment: The patient's new breast cancer diagnosis and receptor results raise concern for a hereditary cancer susceptibility. A focused multigene panel is appropriate because several clinically actionable genes beyond BRCA1 and BRCA2 are associated with hereditary breast cancer.
sections.medicalManagementImpact: A pathogenic germline finding could affect systemic therapy options, including potential eligibility for PARP-directed therapy; influence breast surgical planning and future breast surveillance; prompt risk management for ovarian or other associated cancers; and allow targeted testing and surveillance for relatives.
sections.plan: Recommend a focused germline hereditary breast cancer panel with sequencing and deletion/duplication analysis. Genetic counseling was provided, including possible positive, negative, and uncertain results; protections and limits related to genetic information; and implications for treatment, surveillance, and family members.
sections.geneticCounseling: Provided on 2026-07-03 by the Hereditary Cancer Clinic. Maria demonstrated understanding and elected to proceed with testing.
